frac.unitSplit: One whole, from 0 to 1, is split into {d} equal parts.
frac.unitHops: {n}/{d} is {n, plural, one {# hop} other {# hops}} of 1/{d} from 0.
frac.equiv: {a}/{b} = {an}/{bn}: multiply the numerator and the denominator by {m}.
frac.commonDen: Use the common denominator {l}: it is a multiple of both {b} and {d}.
frac.sameDen: Same denominator {d}: the one with more parts is bigger.
frac.sameNum: Same numerator {n}: the more parts a whole is cut into, the smaller each part.
frac.tenthsWindow: From {lo} to {hi} there are {n} equal parts: each is one tenth.
frac.hundredthsWindow: From {lo} to {hi} there are {n} equal parts: each is one hundredth.
frac.tenthsHops: From {lo}, {n, plural, one {# hop of one tenth reaches} other {# hops of one tenth reach}} {x}.
frac.hundredthsHops: From {lo}, {n, plural, one {# hop of one hundredth reaches} other {# hops of one hundredth reach}} {x}.
frac.decPlaces: Compare the tenths first, then the hundredths.
frac.decTenths: {a} is {an, plural, one {# tenth} other {# tenths}} and {b} is {bn, plural, one {# tenth} other {# tenths}}.
frac.decHundredths: {a} is {an, plural, one {# hundredth} other {# hundredths}} and {b} is {bn, plural, one {# hundredth} other {# hundredths}}.
frac.pctTen: {p}% of {of} is {ten}: that is one hop.
frac.pctThreeQuarters: 75% is three quarters: {of} {op} 4 = {q}, and three of those make {r}.
frac.pctHops: {pct}% is {n, plural, one {# hop} other {# hops}} of 10%: {r}.
frac.pctFive: 5% is half of 10%: half of {ten} is {r}.
frac.pctHopsHalf: {pct}% is {n, plural, one {# hop} other {# hops}} of 10% and half a hop: {r}.

count.off_by_one.name: Counting slip (one too many or few)
count.off_by_one.tip: Count each hop out loud, one at a time.

add.dropped_ten.name: Dropped the ten when bridging 10
add.dropped_ten.tip: When you pass 10, keep the ten!

add.no_carry.name: Forgot to carry
add.no_carry.tip: When a column makes 10 or more, carry the ten to the next column.

add.carry_concat.name: Wrote the whole column sum instead of carrying
add.carry_concat.tip: Write only the ones; carry the ten.

sub.count_includes_start.name: Counted the starting number when counting back
sub.count_includes_start.tip: Don't count the number you start on — count the hops.

sub.smaller_from_larger.name: Subtracted the smaller digit from the larger in each column
sub.smaller_from_larger.tip: If the top digit is smaller, borrow a ten first.

sub.borrow_no_decrement.name: Borrowed without reducing the next column
sub.borrow_no_decrement.tip: When you borrow a ten, the next column goes down by one.

pv.reversal.name: Swapped tens and ones
pv.reversal.tip: Tens come first: big hops of 10, then small hops.

pv.concat.name: Wrote digits side by side without regrouping
pv.concat.tip: Ten ones make a new ten.

pv.missing_zero.name: Left out a zero place holder
pv.missing_zero.tip: An empty place still needs a 0.

bonds.gave_total.name: Gave the total instead of the missing part
bonds.gave_total.tip: Count only the hops to the flag.

bonds.echo.name: Repeated the given number
bonds.echo.tip: Count the hops between you and the flag.

mul.added.name: Added instead of multiplying
mul.added.tip: Times means equal hops, again and again.

mul.adjacent_fact.name: Neighbouring fact (one group too many or few)
mul.adjacent_fact.tip: Count the groups — one more or one less changes the answer.

mul.zeros.name: Wrong number of zeros
mul.zeros.tip: Count the zeros in both numbers.

mul.no_carry.name: Forgot to carry in multiplication
mul.no_carry.tip: Split the number into tens and ones, then add the parts.

mul.partial_products_missing.name: Multiplied tens by tens and ones by ones only

div.subtracted.name: Subtracted instead of dividing
div.subtracted.tip: Count how many equal hops reach the flag.

div.off_by_one.name: One hop too many or few

int.sign_error.name: Right size, wrong sign
int.sign_error.tip: Check which side of 0 you end up on.

int.sub_neg_as_sub.name: Treated minus a negative as minus
int.sub_neg_as_sub.tip: Minus a negative means hop right.

int.added_magnitudes.name: Added the sizes and kept the minus
int.added_magnitudes.tip: From a negative number, adding moves you right, toward 0.

biggerDen.name: Thought a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
biggerDen.tip: A bigger denominator means smaller parts: 1/8 is less than 1/4.

countedTicks.name: Counted the tick marks instead of the parts
countedTicks.tip: Count the hops between the ticks, not the ticks themselves.

addSame.name: Added the same number to the numerator and the denominator
addSame.tip: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number; adding changes the fraction.

numeratorOnly.name: Looked only at the numerator
numeratorOnly.tip: The denominator matters too: it tells you how big each part is.

wholeLine.name: Split the whole line instead of one whole
wholeLine.tip: One whole is the space from 0 to 1. Split that, not the whole line.

longerIsLarger.name: Thought more digits means a bigger number
longerIsLarger.tip: Compare the tenths first: 0.5 = 0.50, which is more than 0.45.

shorterIsLarger.name: Thought fewer digits means a bigger number
shorterIsLarger.tip: Give both the same number of decimals: 0.3 = 0.30, which is less than 0.45.

misaligned.name: Lined up the last digits instead of the decimal points
misaligned.tip: Line up the decimal points: tenths under tenths, hundredths under hundredths.

tenthsAsHundredths.name: Mixed up tenths and hundredths
tenthsAsHundredths.tip: The first digit after the point is tenths, the second is hundredths. Ten tenths make one whole.

asNumber.name: Gave the percent itself as the answer
asNumber.tip: A percent is a part of 100. Find 10% first, then build up.

dividedBy.name: Divided by the percent
dividedBy.tip: Percent means out of 100: 10% of 80 is 80 ÷ 10 = 8.

mastery.add20.name: Twenty Tamer
mastery.add20.desc: You can add any two numbers within 20.

mastery.times.name: Table Master
mastery.times.desc: The whole times table is yours.

mastery.bridge.name: Bridge Crosser
mastery.bridge.desc: You mastered a skill from the next level up.
mastery.bridge.hint: Master a skill above your level.

persist.streak3.name: Three in a Row
persist.streak3.hint: Play three days in a row.

persist.streak7.name: Habit Hatched
persist.streak7.desc: A whole week — this is a habit now.
persist.streak7.hint: Play seven days in a row.

persist.comeback.name: Welcome Back
persist.comeback.desc: You came back after a break. Good to see you!
persist.comeback.hint: Come back after a few days away.

persist.dayAfterHard.name: Sunrise
persist.dayAfterHard.desc: Yesterday was tough, and you came back today.
persist.dayAfterHard.hint: Play the day after a tough session.
persist.dayAfterHard.desc@C: Trained the day after a hard session.

explore.switchMid.name: Switcheroo
explore.switchMid.desc: You switched language in the middle of a game.

explore.stretch.name: Mountain Goat
explore.stretch.desc@C: Completed items on the challenge path.

explore.strands.name: Explorer
explore.strands.desc: You practised three different kinds of maths.

resil.fixOne.name: Second Go
resil.fixOne.desc: Wrong the first time, right the next. That's learning.
resil.fixOne.hint: Get a problem right when it comes back.
resil.fixOne.desc@C: Fixed an error on the retry.

resil.thirdTry.name: Third Time's the Charm
resil.thirdTry.desc: Right on the third try. You didn't give up.
resil.thirdTry.hint: Get a problem right after missing it twice.

resil.fourthTry.name: Unstoppable
resil.fourthTry.desc: Wrong three times — then right. Amazing persistence.
resil.fourthTry.hint: Get a problem right after missing it three times.

resil.finishedHard.name: Tough Cookie
resil.finishedHard.desc: That session was hard, and you finished it.
resil.finishedHard.hint: Finish a session even when it's hard.

resil.returned.name: Boomerang
resil.returned.desc: You came back to a skill that was tricky before.
resil.returned.hint: Come back to a skill you found hard.
resil.returned.desc@C: Returned to a skill after a rough day.

resil.fixed25.name: Mistake Mechanic
resil.fixed25.desc: Twenty-five mistakes fixed. Mistakes are how brains grow.

secret.palindrome.name: Mirror Number
secret.palindrome.desc: Your answer reads the same backwards!

secret.bullseye.name: Bullseye
secret.bullseye.desc: An estimate that was exactly right.

secret.sameAnswer.name: Déjà Vu
secret.sameAnswer.desc: The same answer three times in a row!

secret.weekend.name: Weekend Warrior
secret.weekend.desc: You played on Saturday and on Sunday.

secret.marathonFrog.name: Marathon Frog
secret.marathonFrog.desc: A thousand hops! Pip needs a nap.

frac.biggerFrac: Which fraction is bigger? Land on it.
frac.smallerFrac: Which fraction is smaller? Land on it.
frac.biggerDec: Which number is bigger? Land on it.
frac.smallerDec: Which number is smaller? Land on it.
frac.read: Which number is at the flag? Type it.
frac.equiv: Which number goes in the numerator?
frac.percent: How much is that? Type the number.

hint.hop: The first hop goes from {from} to {to}.

s.count: Count each dot exactly once. Small groups make it easier.
s.locateTens: Jump in tens first, then in ones.
s.locateHundreds: Jump in hundreds first, then in tens, then in ones.
s.locateNeg: Negative numbers are to the left of zero, positive numbers to the right.
s.blocks2: Count the tens first, then the ones.
s.blocks3: Count the hundreds first, then the tens, then the ones.
s.bond: Count on from the first number until you reach the total.
s.makeTen: Make a ten first, then add what is left.
s.makeTen@C: Bridge through ten: complete the ten, then add the remainder.
s.backThroughTen: Go back to ten first, then take away what is left.
s.backThroughTen@C: Bridge back through ten: subtract down to ten, then subtract the remainder.
s.countOn: Start at the bigger number and count on.
s.countBack: Start at the first number and count back.

split.add: Split the second number by place value, then add one part at a time.
split.add@C: Decompose the second addend by place value and add the parts one at a time.
split.sub: Split the number you take away by place value, then subtract one part at a time.
split.sub@C: Decompose the subtrahend by place value and subtract the parts one at a time.
split.mul: Split one number by place value, multiply each part, then add the results.
split.mul@C: Distributive law: split one factor by place value, multiply each part, then add the products.

step.add: Start at the first number and hop forward by the second.
step.sub: Start at the first number and hop back by the second.

s.times9: Nines: work out ten groups, then take one group away.
s.times9@C: Nines: ten groups minus one group.
s.doubleDouble: Times four: double, then double again.
s.fivePlus: Do five groups first, then the rest of the groups, and add them together.
s.fivePlus@C: Split the first factor into five plus the rest, then add the two products.
s.repeatedAdd: Multiplying is adding equal groups: make equal hops, one after another.
s.divAsHops: Think times tables: what do you multiply the second number by to get the first?
s.divAsHops@C: Division undoes multiplication: find the missing factor.
s.timesTen: Multiplying by ten moves every digit one place to the left; by a hundred, two places.
s.zeros: Set the zeros aside, multiply what is left, then put all the zeros back.
s.addPartials: Work out each part, then add the parts together.
s.subNeg: Taking away a negative number is the same as adding the positive number.
s.subNeg@C: Subtracting a negative number means adding its opposite.
s.addNeg: Adding a negative number is the same as taking away the positive number.
s.addNeg@C: Adding a negative number means subtracting its opposite.
s.intMove: On the number line, adding takes you to the right and taking away to the left.
s.generic: Picture it on the number line: where do you start, and which way do you hop?

storage.otherTab: Hopa is already open in another browser tab or window, so nothing is saved here. Close Hopa there, then reload this page.
storage.idbUsed: Answer history: {kb} KB in the browser's database, with room for years of play.
storage.localOnly: The browser's database is not available, so the answer history stays in the storage above; when it fills up, the oldest months are summarised.
storage.historyHidden: Older answer history could not be opened this time. Nothing is lost: reload the page. A backup made now would not include it.
storage.persisted: Protected: the browser will not clear this data to free up space.
storage.notPersisted: The browser may clear this data if the device runs low on space.
storage.keepSafeDenied: The browser has not allowed it yet. Adding Hopa to the Home Screen and regular backups also keep the data safe.
